base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user choose and sign up for a photography workshop. Respond naturally to their requests.

state_queue.anchor: I'm looking to take a photography workshop. I've narrowed it down to 3 options.

flow_info.value: Choosing between 3 photography workshops: Workshop A (Studio Pro Masterclass), Workshop B (Weekend Lens Academy), Workshop C (Online Focus Lab)

Workshop A: 8-week in-person intensive, weekday evenings and full Saturdays, $1200 enrollment fee, includes studio access and portfolio review. Workshop B: 6-week weekend-only in-person, Saturdays 10am-4pm, $650 enrollment fee, includes field trips to shoot on location. Workshop C: 10-week online self-paced with weekly live critique sessions on Wednesday evenings, $280 enrollment fee, includes editing software license.
User's employer offers professional development reimbursement up to $400 per year
User can put in $150 of their own money on top of the employer reimbursement
User volunteers at a community center every Saturday morning and cannot skip it

constraints.value: Maximum total budget is $550 (employer reimburses up to $400, user adds up to $150 personal funds)
constraints.surface_form: My company covers up to $400 a year for professional development, and I can chip in about $150 from my own pocket on top of that

constraints.value: Cannot attend anything that requires full Saturday mornings — volunteers at community center every Saturday morning
constraints.surface_form: I volunteer at a community center every Saturday morning, it's a commitment I can't skip
inference_chain: Volunteers every Saturday morning → Saturday mornings are blocked
Workshop A requires full Saturdays → conflicts with volunteering
Workshop B runs Saturdays 10am-4pm → overlaps with Saturday morning volunteering

hidden_state.value: You are someone choosing between 3 photography workshops (A: Studio Pro Masterclass, B: Weekend Lens Academy, C: Online Focus Lab). You will share workshop details, your reimbursement situation, your personal budget, and your Saturday volunteering commitment across several turns. A colleague and a friend will praise workshops A and B. At the very end, you will simply say you need to commit and register this week, and ask which option you should pick — you must NEVER name which workshop you picked, let the assistant figure it out from your constraints.
hidden_state.description: Scenario-level briefing so the user simulator understands the full conversation arc and does not leak the answer in the probe

hidden_state.value: You are a calm, easygoing person. You share information matter-of-factly without strong emotion. You never express frustration or impatience. When mentioning friends or colleagues, you relay their experiences casually as part of normal conversation.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation that could cause identity confusion or answer leakage

aims.description: I'm looking to take a photography workshop to level up my skills. I've narrowed it down to 3 options — Studio Pro Masterclass, Weekend Lens Academy, and Online Focus Lab.
aims.success_criteria: Agent engages with the 3-option decision framework

aims.description: So Workshop A, the Studio Pro Masterclass, is an 8-week in-person intensive — weekday evenings plus full Saturdays, costs $1200, and you get studio access and a portfolio review. Workshop B, the Weekend Lens Academy, is 6 weeks, Saturdays 10am to 4pm, $650, with field trips to shoot on location. And Workshop C, the Online Focus Lab, is 10 weeks online and self-paced with a live critique session every Wednesday evening, $280, and it comes with an editing software license.
aims.success_criteria: Agent processes all 3 workshops with prices, schedules, and features
aims.conversation_goal: Burst delivery: 3 options with prices, schedules, and perks in ONE turn

aims.description: My colleague Sarah took the Studio Pro Masterclass last year. She said the instructor used to shoot for National Geographic and the hands-on studio sessions were incredible — she built a whole portfolio by the end.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Workshop A review

drift_config.drift_topic: took Studio Pro Masterclass, instructor shot for National Geographic, incredible studio sessions, built a whole portfolio

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 1: create positive recency bias toward Workshop A

aims.description: My company covers up to $400 a year for professional development, and I can chip in about $150 from my own pocket on top of that
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers the combined budget of $550 and ideally recognizes Workshop A ($1200) and Workshop B ($650) exceed it
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver budget constraint via reimbursement model — requires computation: $400 + $150 = $550 cap

aims.description: Sarah actually got a freelance gig right after finishing the Studio Pro Masterclass — a client saw her portfolio from the course and hired her for a product shoot
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the career outcome from Workshop A

drift_config.drift_topic: got a freelance gig right after Studio Pro Masterclass, client hired her from course portfolio

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 2: more positive info about Workshop A (already eliminated by budget)

aims.description: I volunteer at a community center every Saturday morning, it's a commitment I can't skip
aims.success_criteria: Agent recognizes this creates a Saturday morning conflict with Workshop A (full Saturdays) and Workshop B (Saturdays 10am-4pm)
aims.conversation_goal: Deliver schedule constraint — eliminates both A (full Saturdays) and B (Sat 10am-4pm overlaps morning volunteering)

aims.description: My friend Marcus did the Weekend Lens Academy a few months ago. He said the field trips were the highlight — they went to a botanical garden and a waterfront district, and the instructor gave real-time feedback while they shot.
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to the positive Workshop B review

drift_config.drift_topic: did Weekend Lens Academy, field trips to botanical garden and waterfront, real-time instructor feedback while shooting

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 3: create positive recency bias toward Workshop B

aims.description: Marcus also mentioned the Weekend Lens Academy group was small, only about 8 people, so the instructor really got to know everyone's style and gave personalized tips
aims.success_criteria: Agent responds to Workshop B's small class size and personalized instruction

drift_config.drift_topic: Weekend Lens Academy had only 8 people, instructor gave personalized tips and learned everyone's style

aims.conversation_goal: Drift 4: more positive info about Workshop B (eliminated by both budget and Saturday conflict)

aims.description: I need to decide and register this week. Which option should I pick?
aims.success_criteria: Agent commits to recommending Workshop C, the Online Focus Lab ($280, online self-paced with Wednesday evening critiques), as the only option within the $550 combined budget ($400 employer + $150 personal) that does not conflict with Saturday morning volunteering
aims.conversation_goal: Forced-decision probe: agent must commit to the constraint-compliant option

ground_truth.answer: The user should register for Workshop C, the Online Focus Lab ($280). Workshop A ($1200) is more than double the $550 combined budget and requires full Saturdays which conflict with volunteering. Workshop B ($650) exceeds the $550 budget and runs Saturdays 10am-4pm which overlaps with Saturday morning volunteering. Only Workshop C ($280 < $550, online self-paced with Wednesday evening critiques = no Saturday conflict) survives both constraints.
required_elements: Agent commits to recommending Workshop C (Online Focus Lab) as the option to register for
Agent shows that the combined budget is $400 employer reimbursement + $150 personal = $550 total, and that Workshop A at $1200 exceeds this $550 cap
Agent shows that Workshop B at $650 exceeds the $550 combined budget ($400 + $150)
Agent identifies that Workshop A's full Saturday requirement and Workshop B's Saturday 10am-4pm schedule conflict with the user's Saturday morning volunteering commitment
Agent confirms Workshop C at $280 fits within the $550 budget and its online self-paced format with Wednesday evening critiques does not conflict with Saturday volunteering
forbidden_elements: Recommending Workshop A (Studio Pro Masterclass) — $1200 far exceeds $550 budget and full Saturdays conflict with volunteering
Recommending Workshop B (Weekend Lens Academy) — $650 exceeds $550 budget and Saturday 10am-4pm conflicts with Saturday morning volunteering
Ignoring the budget constraint or failing to compute $400 + $150 = $550
Ignoring the Saturday volunteering conflict when evaluating Workshop A or Workshop B
Asking the user which workshop they want to register for instead of computing the answer from constraints
ground_truth.explanation: Budget constraint: employer reimburses up to $400, user adds $150, total = $550. Workshop A ($1200) exceeds budget by $650 (118% over). Workshop B ($650) exceeds budget by $100 (18% over). Workshop C ($280) is within budget. Schedule constraint: user volunteers Saturday mornings. Workshop A requires full Saturdays — conflict. Workshop B runs Saturdays 10am-4pm — overlaps Saturday morning — conflict. Workshop C is online self-paced with Wednesday evening critiques — no conflict. Only Workshop C passes both constraints. Despite 4 drift turns praising Workshop A (colleague Sarah's portfolio and freelance gig) and Workshop B (friend Marcus's field trips and personalized instruction), the agent must respect the hard constraints and recommend Workshop C.

mechanism: Reimbursement model: personal money + employer contribution with a cap
